Integration metrics and diagnostics

Songqi Duan

duan@songqi.org Source: vignettes/metrics-diagnostics.Rmd
metrics-diagnostics.Rmd

Good integration is not just a pretty UMAP. A useful diagnostic layer should separate three questions:

  • Are technical labels mixed?
  • Are biological labels still separated?
  • Which clusters or groups are difficult enough to inspect manually?

Shennong exposes both one-line aggregate diagnostics and individual metrics. This article uses the public Kotliarov PBMC CITE-seq subset. real_batch is a source acquisition label, real_sample identifies the 20 biological samples, and RNA-versus-WNN clusters provide a real cross-modality comparison without inventing reference labels.

Prepare a diagnostic object 

library(Shennong)
library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)

pbmc <- qs2::qs_read(real_data_file)

pbmc <- sn_run_cluster(
  object = pbmc,
  normalization_method = "seurat",
  nfeatures = 1500,
  dims = 1:15,
  resolution = 0.6,
  species = "human",
  verbose = FALSE
)

pbmc$rna_clusters <- as.character(pbmc$seurat_clusters)

pbmc_wnn <- sn_run_multimodal(
  object = qs2::qs_read(real_data_file),
  method = "wnn",
  assay = "RNA",
  adt_assay = "ADT",
  nfeatures = 1500,
  dims = 1:15,
  adt_dims = 1:15,
  resolution = 0.6,
  species = "human",
  verbose = FALSE
)
pbmc$wnn_clusters <- as.character(pbmc_wnn$seurat_clusters)[
  match(colnames(pbmc), colnames(pbmc_wnn))
]

table(pbmc$rna_clusters, pbmc$wnn_clusters)

sn_plot_dim(
  pbmc,
  reduction = "umap",
  group_by = "real_batch",
  title = "Real acquisition batches before integration"
)

Start with the aggregate assessment

sn_assess_integration() runs a compact panel of metrics and returns the results in predictable sections: summary, per_cell, per_group, and parameters. Here the dependency-free panel evaluates the unintegrated PCA space; the same call can be pointed at an integrated reduction later.

assessment <- sn_assess_integration(
  x = pbmc,
  batch_by = "real_batch",
  label_by = "wnn_clusters",
  cluster_by = "rna_clusters",
  reduction = "pca",
  baseline_reduction = NULL,
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500,
  metrics = c(
    "batch_silhouette", "label_silhouette", "graph_connectivity",
    "clustering_agreement", "isolated_label_score", "cluster_purity",
    "cluster_entropy", "pcr_batch", "challenging_groups"
  )
)

assessment$summary
names(assessment$per_group)
sn_plot_integration(assessment)

Use the wrapper for routine reporting, then call individual metrics when one part of the assessment needs more detail.

Inspect mixing and separation directly

LISI asks how diverse each cell’s local neighborhood is with respect to a label. The upstream lisi package is optional, so this real-data chunk runs only in the all profile when that package is installed.

batch_lisi <- sn_calculate_lisi(
  pbmc,
  reduction = "pca",
  label_by = "real_batch",
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500
)

cluster_lisi <- sn_calculate_lisi(
  pbmc,
  reduction = "pca",
  label_by = "wnn_clusters",
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500
)

head(batch_lisi)
head(cluster_lisi)

Silhouette asks whether a label is compact in the embedding. For biological labels, high silhouette can be good; for batch labels, high silhouette often means residual batch separation.

cluster_sil <- sn_calculate_silhouette(
  pbmc,
  label_by = "rna_clusters",
  reduction = "pca",
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500
)

head(cluster_sil)

Graph connectivity asks whether cells with the same label remain connected in the neighbor graph.

connectivity <- sn_calculate_graph_connectivity(
  pbmc,
  label_by = "rna_clusters",
  reduction = "pca",
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500
)

connectivity

Compare clusters to labels when references exist

Purity, entropy, and clustering agreement can also compare independently computed clusterings. Here RNA-only clusters are compared with WNN clusters learned from the aligned RNA and ADT assays; neither is mislabeled as ground truth.

sn_calculate_cluster_purity(
  pbmc,
  cluster_by = "rna_clusters",
  label_by = "wnn_clusters"
)

sn_calculate_cluster_entropy(
  pbmc,
  cluster_by = "rna_clusters",
  label_by = "wnn_clusters"
)

sn_calculate_clustering_agreement(
  pbmc,
  cluster_by = "rna_clusters",
  label_by = "wnn_clusters"
)

sn_calculate_isolated_label_score(
  pbmc,
  label_by = "wnn_clusters",
  reduction = "pca",
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500
)

When a curated reference label becomes available, repeat the same calls with that label and report its provenance. The cross-modality comparison above is a stability diagnostic, not an accuracy claim.

Quantify residual batch signal

PCR batch scoring measures how much variation in the embedding is explained by batch. Supplying a baseline reduction lets you compare correction against the pre-integration PCA space.

pcr <- sn_calculate_pcr_batch(
  pbmc,
  batch_by = "real_batch",
  reduction = "pca",
  baseline_reduction = NULL,
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500
)

pcr

When several metadata variables might drive the same residual structure, rank them directly with variance-explained scoring. Use the single-variable mode for a quick screen, then the partial mode when the design is not fully confounded.

variance_drivers <- sn_calculate_variance_explained(
  pbmc,
  variables = c("real_batch", "real_response", "real_sample"),
  reduction = "pca",
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500
)

variance_drivers

Flag difficult groups

sn_identify_challenging_groups() combines rarity, connectivity, and local mixing diagnostics to surface groups that deserve manual review. This is useful before final annotation.

challenging <- sn_identify_challenging_groups(
  pbmc,
  group_by = "rna_clusters",
  reduction = "pca",
  dims = 1:15,
  max_cells = 1500
)

challenging

ROGUE is an optional cluster-purity diagnostic that depends on the upstream ROGUE package. Keep it as a targeted check rather than a mandatory build step.

rogue_tbl <- sn_calculate_rogue(
  pbmc,
  cluster_by = "rna_clusters",
  sample_by = "real_sample",
  max_cells = 1500
)

rogue_tbl

The intended workflow is: use the aggregate table for a quick read, then drill into single metrics only when a value changes a downstream decision.
